mcat_description.short: Glass Cabin refers to a prefabricated or site-assembled enclosure with toughened glass panels set in aluminium or steel frames, primarily used to create partitioned office workspaces, manager cabins, or semi-enclosed rooms within larger commercial interiors.
mcat_description.long: Glass Cabins in the Indian B2B market are modular enclosures constructed using toughened safety glass (typically 6mm–12mm thick, IS 2553-compliant) mounted in powder-coated or anodised aluminium section frames, used to partition open-plan offices into individual workstations or manager cabins. The dominant commercial form is the aluminium-framed office cabin supplied and installed on a per-square-foot basis, with customisation in glass thickness, frame finish, door type (swing or sliding), and glazing style (full glass, half glass/half solid, or frameless). Secondary variants include portable standalone glass cabins for outdoor or terrace use, security/guard booths with glass panels, and bath/shower enclosures — though these represent a minority of demand. Key glass types used include clear toughened, tinted, frosted, reflective, and laminated glass, with Saint-Gobain being the most cited brand in the Indian market.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, 'Glass Cabin' is the dominant trade term for aluminium-framed toughened glass office partition enclosures, used interchangeably with 'glass partition cabin' and 'aluminium office cabin' by both buyers and sellers. The product is supplied and installed on a per-square-foot basis by aluminium fabricators and interior fit-out contractors, with the aluminium section profile (typically 35x50mm or 25x45mm) and glass thickness (6mm, 8mm, 10mm, 12mm) being the primary differentiating specifications. Toughened safety glass used in these cabins must comply with IS 2553 (Part 1): 2018, which classifies safety glass into toughened and laminated types with specifications on thickness and impact resistance; BIS certification for safety glass became mandatory under the Safety Glass Quality Control Order effective April 2023. Saint-Gobain is the most prominently cited glass brand in the Indian office cabin market, with powder-coated and anodised aluminium finishes being the two dominant frame surface treatments. The category sits within the broader prefabricated structures taxonomy but is functionally closer to interior fit-out/partitioning than to portable cabin structures — a distinction that creates listing contamination risk from both glass partition products (flat panels without enclosure) and portable steel/FRP cabins.
